lines.x: Smaller oil tankers moved record volumes out of the Strait of Hormuz in October as Iran targeted supertankers, while regional vessel attacks and Middle East tensions kept energy markets volatile.
Brent crude held steady near $92 per barrel as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz offset expectations of a global supply surplus.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported two commercial oil tankers suffered damage from unidentified projectiles near Khasab, Oman, including one hit directly in the engine room.
Oil prices declined after US crude and fuel inventories rose, though losses were limited by ongoing US-Iran clashes and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
